Subject: Follow-up: DPA & SCC selection from today's call

Hi Jane

Thanks for the time on the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we don't lose momentum: 

Summary from our side:
- Acme is evaluating Redwood for customer-facing features that will process EU personal data (user profiles + usage telemetry).
- You flagged GDPR requirements, the need for a signed DPA, SCCs for international transfers, and confirmation of Redwood's SOC 2 status.
- You also asked for us to complete your vendor security questionnaire (VSA).

Proposed next steps (we can adjust):
1) I attached our draft DPA for initial review (Redwood_DPA_draft_20260905.pdf). Please confirm whether you intend to be the Controller and Redwood the Processor for these activities. If Acme requires Redwood to act as Controller for any specific processing, call that out and we can escalate.
2) SCC module selection: based on call, it sounds like Acme will be Controller and Redwood the Processor. If so, Module 2 (Controller-to-Processor) is the usual pick. I attached an SCC-module-mapping spreadsheet that shows recommended selection and rationale.
3) SOC 2: our latest SOC 2 Type II report is available
we can share it under NDA. Please confirm the right contact/email to send to, or we can upload to your secure portal.
4) Vendor security questionnaire: we can start answering your VSA; please send the questionnaire or a link and let us know which sections are highest priority (privacy, encryption, retention, subprocessors).

Requested timeline: if possible, could we get Acme's legal review of the DPA and SCC preference by EOD 9/8? Rishi and I will prepare a redline-ready version if you want tracked changes.

Cc'ing Rishi (sales lead) and Monica (security & compliance) to own follow-ups.

Thanks

look forward to next steps.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks Marissa

Helpful summary. A few quick notes: 

- Controller/Processor: Acme will be Controller for customer data. Redwood will be Processor. We do not foresee Redwood acting as Controller for the scoped processing.
- SCC modules: we generally expect Controller-to-Processor clauses. From a practical standpoint our legal team prefers Module 2 (Controller-to-Processor) unless Redwood is transferring data on its own behalf. Please confirm you are comfortable with Module 2.
- SOC 2: please send the SOC 2 Type II report to legal@acme.com. We'll treat it as confidential under our vendor intake process.
- VSA: I'll upload the questionnaire tonight to your HubSpot link and flag 3 high-priority sections: encryption at rest/in transit, subprocessors, and data retention.

We should be able to get initial comments on the DPA by 9/8, but if we have substantive redlines we may need a short follow-up call with legal.

Best,
Jane Doe
Senior Counsel, Acme Analytics
jane.doe@acme.com
